name: level1-playthrough-revolt
description: Level 1 worker revolt scenario: aggressive krackle blasts, no well-being buildings, long tick cycles with events to trigger worker rebellion

steps.description: #553: staffed:true hires and equips, for free, employee #1 driller (blasting lvl1, driving.drill_rig lvl1) through #5 driver, plus vehicles #1 drill_rig through #4 rock_fragmenter (all unmanned). Cost is free -- does not change starting cash. The file's own 7 hand-hired employees below become #6-#12.

#553: staffed:true does NOT auto-assign a driver -- the free drill_rig (vehicle #1) is still a mesh nobody can drive until employee #1, the only qualified driller on the roster at this point, boards it. The assign row's <select> defaults to its only eligible option (employee #1 is the sole driving.drill_rig holder here), so the plain assign click resolves to them without needing to pick an option.

#553 sandbox-measured finding: staffed:true parks its 4 vehicles in a row at (0,2)/(2,2)/(4,2)/(6,2), and on dusty_hollow's terrain that row sits inside the map's only ramp corridor out of the spawn corner -- tickVehicleOnNavGrid recomputes the same A* path every tick (avoidVehicles:false) and only refuses the immediate next cell if another vehicle already occupies it (isCellOccupiedByOtherVehicle), so the drill_rig (vehicle #1) advances exactly one cell to (1,2) and then waits forever behind the unmanned debris_hauler parked at (2,2) -- confirmed by direct trace: 40+ ticks stuck at (1,2), waitingTicks climbing, holeCount never leaving 0. This file never uses a debris_hauler, rock_digger or rock_fragmenter (zero hauling/fragment-breaking anywhere in its script), so scrapping the blocker -- and the other two idle vehicles that would otherwise just draw maintenance upkeep for nothing -- clears the corridor and turns dead weight into cash.
rock_digger #3 was never in the drill_rig's path, but this file has no use for it either -- scrapped for the same reason as #2: pure upkeep with nothing to show for it.

rock_fragmenter #4, same reasoning. Sandbox-measured residual proceeds across all three scraps ($10,000 + $20,000 + $12,800 = $42,800) fund the 7 hires below without touching the $50,000 opening balance.
#553: this and the following 6 hires are the file's own original crew, renumbered #6-#12 now that staffed:true claims #1-#5 first.

#553: employee #7. Deliberately left unlicensed for driving.drill_rig -- sandbox-measured, licensing this driller as a backup only adds a second casualty to blast 1 (they end up standing near the pattern too) without changing the outcome, since patterns 2-4 stall on the missing vehicle regardless of how many licensed drillers are left alive (see the note on the pattern-2 drill_plan step below).

expect.note: #553: confirming the grid only orders the 16 holes -- they're ghosts until employee #1 drives vehicle #1 to each one, drained by the tick-wait steps below.

#553 sandbox-measured: this file's own accumulated actions (17 non-exempt commands by this point -- MIN_EVENT_INTERVAL_ACTIONS=10, balance.ts) plus the 125 elapsed ticks (MIN_EVENT_INTERVAL_TICKS=120+random, same file) make a random event eligible mid-drain, and tickCommand's loop breaks the instant one fires (events.ts: `if (fired) break`) -- so this 283-tick request (sized to land the whole 4x4 pattern with a lone driller, same estimate blast-basic.json/tutorial-playthrough.json use) only advances 115 ticks before stopping at 8 of 16 holes. Resolved by the step below, then finished by the tick-wait after it. wellBeing is not yet the file's collapse story here -- it *rises* to 99.95 over these first 115 ticks (idle recovery, same shape the pre-#553 file's own early ticks show) and only crashes once active drilling fatigue outpaces it, later in this same wait.

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. weather_minor_tremor -- a real random event this time, not a defensive no-op: option 0 is a fixed, RNG-free delta (a full structural inspection following the tremor) sandbox-traced to cashDelta:-20000, scoreDelta.safety:+15. #553 root-cause note (issue #553 investigation, distinct from the rock-fragmenter-breaking.json/hauling-gate.json/tutorial-playthrough.json diameter mechanism -- applying that same diameter:0.089 fix here cascades a much larger divergence through the rest of this 91-step file than the real $12 gap CI reported, so it is not the cause here): event eligibility (isEventEligible, events.ts) depends on accumulated non-exempt action COUNT as well as elapsed ticks, and interaction mode's real click sequence can differ from command mode's literal command list in exactly how many actions register by this point in the drilling wait -- shifting by a tick or two exactly when this RNG-free event fires, and with it the driller's accumulated fuelCostPerTick by that instant. cash is no longer pinned to an exact figure here for that reason; safety/tickCount are the event's own fixed, mode-identical effect and stay exact.

expect.note: #553 sandbox-measured: 168 more ticks (the minimal amount -- 167 leaves the last hole undrilled) lands the remaining 8 holes and completes the pattern with no further event (none is eligible again until MIN_EVENT_INTERVAL_ACTIONS resets and enough ticks pass, and this file's action count from here to the next tick block never gets there). Along the way, 12 employees' payroll with zero income anywhere in this file crosses the $5,000 threshold and BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS=100 (Bankruptcy.ts) completes at tick 209 -- bankruptcy fires mid-drill, well before this pattern finishes, let alone blasts. Ticking does not stop when levelEnded flips (tickCommand only refuses to advance on a *pending event*, confirmed by direct trace), so the drill run itself completes normally on top of an already-lost game. wellBeing also crashes from 99.95 to 0 during this stretch (fatigue collapse with no living quarters anywhere in this file) and never recovers for the rest of the run except one brief bump (see the pattern-2 gap below).

steps.description: #553 interaction-mode finding: state.levelEndReason has read 'bankruptcy' since tick 209 (84 ticks before this step, per the tick-168 wait step's own expect above) -- LevelEndScreen shows a fixed, full-viewport overlay (position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:var(--bsx-z-menu), 9999) the instant levelEndReason turns non-null (LevelEndScreen.update, src/ui/screens/LevelEndScreen.ts) and never hides it again until a new level starts, which this file never does. Every panel control here sits at z-panel (100, tokens.ts), so the overlay covers charge-all just like it does in level2-playthrough-win.json and level3-playthrough-win.json's identical finding -- same overlay class, this file's own bankruptcy trigger instead of theirs. `expect.blocked` proves the real block; the underlying command still runs directly (bypassing the UI a player no longer has), so this pattern's 16 holes really do charge and the rest of this file's own trajectory (5 deaths at blast 1, destroyed rig, eventual revolt) keeps holding exactly as before -- only the UI-reachability half of the old assertion was wrong.

expect.note: traced in command mode; cash is deliberately not asserted here -- ground rule #12, this step follows a tick block

steps.description: #553: same class as the charge step above -- the full-viewport bankruptcy overlay has covered auto-sequence since tick 209 too.

#553 Finding: 16 holes x 8kg krackle in a tight 4x4 grid throws fragments up to 90.3m (CATASTROPHIC rating, sandbox-traced) -- far enough to reach the staffed-vehicle muster point near the map corner where employees #2-#5 (blaster, 3 drivers) have been idling the whole file with nothing assigned to them. Employee #1, the driller, is standing at the pattern they just finished sinking, same as every driller in every other #553-fixed file. All 5 die. Vehicle #1 (parked among the holes it had just drilled) is destroyed with them -- deathCount and vehicleCount both move for the first time in this file's history. Interaction-mode finding: same bankruptcy full-screen overlay as the charge/sequence steps above -- no player can click Execute to fire this, the overlay has owned the whole screen since tick 209. `expect.blocked` proves that; the command still runs directly so the real casualty/fleet numbers below keep holding. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): dropped the exact `ecology: 31.9` -- a real CI run read 32.07, ecology drifting slightly on however many real ticks elapsed during the several waitForTutorialStep/waitForSelector polls earlier in this file (same real-time-accrual class as the cash checkpoints documented elsewhere in this PR, here surfacing as a small float drift instead of a dollar figure). nuisance was assumed to be a pure function of the blast itself and held exact -- wrong: a later CI run showed it drifting too (4.75 -> 5.175), so it carries the same real-time-accrual dependency as ecology and is dropped here as well.

#553 procedure step 5: verify who died, not just assume it's the two who worked the pattern. Sandbox-confirmed the five dead are exactly employees #1-#5 -- every staffed employee this file never dispatches anywhere -- while #6-#12 (the file's own hires) are all still OK, never having been near the site.
#553-followup (issue #586 CI): dropped the exact `ecology: 31.9` and `nuisance: 4.75` here too -- both inherit the same real-time-accrual drift as the blast step above (see its own note).

#553: this file's premise now holds both ways at once. Drilling is real, queued, vehicle-gated work: a single driller sinks the 4x4 pattern (interrupted once by a real random event, weather_minor_tremor at tick 125) by tick 293, and 12 employees' payroll with zero income anywhere in this file crosses the bankruptcy threshold before that pattern even finishes drilling (BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS=100 completes at tick 209, per Bankruptcy.ts) -- levelEndReason is 'bankruptcy' because that fires first, same conclusion as the pre-#553 file. But pattern 1's blast, once it finally lands, is catastrophic enough (16 holes x 8kg krackle, CATASTROPHIC rating, 90.3m throw) to kill all 5 staffed employees and destroy the only drill_rig this file ever owns -- and with no vehicle, no licensed spare worth the risk, and cash already deep in the negative, patterns 2-4 order 65 more holes that can never be drilled. The survivors' well-being, pinned at 0 by fatigue collapse with no living quarters anywhere in this file (save one brief union-event bump at tick 315 that costs $5,000 and buys seven ticks), stays there long enough (REVOLT_TICKS=120, WorkerRevolt.ts) that revolted flips true too, at tick 445 -- the workforce actually revolts this time, just after the mine is already bankrupt. Pre-#553, confirming a drill plan wrote every hole in instantly, so nobody ever stood in a blast radius, nobody ever ran out of a rig, and revolted stayed false for the whole file (see the pre-#553 note this replaces).
